statement: How many lines can a square be folded along so that the two halves match exactly?

choices.misconception: I found the fold down the middle and stopped looking for others.
I found the two straight folds and missed the two corner-to-corner folds.
I found three folds and missed the fourth.
I counted each fold twice, once for each direction.

hints: Try folding sideways, downwards, and corner to corner.
Fold the square in every way you can think of: down the middle one way, the other way, and across each pair of opposite corners. Count only the folds where the halves match exactly.
Two folds go through the middle of the sides and two go through opposite corners.

solutions.reliable: A square matches itself when folded down the middle vertically, horizontally, and along each of its two diagonals, which is 4 folds. The idea to keep: look for folds through sides and through corners, because stopping at the obvious ones is how folds get missed.

whyOnTest: Missing the diagonal folds is almost universal, and the answers for one, two and three folds are all offered.
author: Devansh Sanghavi
